title: release.yml's registry-verification step false-fails on win32-arm64 propagation lag
description: The 'Verify the registry serves what was published' step in .github/workflows/release.yml (release.yml:165-190) polls npm for all seven packages up to 10 times with a fixed 30s sleep (5 minutes total, no backoff), then hard-fails the whole workflow run if any package -- so far always quest-win32-arm64 -- is still not visible. This is now 2 for 2 across real releases (0.4.0 and 0.5.0): the underlying npm publish succeeded both times and the package was live minutes later, but the CI run itself is marked red, which is exactly the failure mode the step's own comment (release.yml:160-164) says it exists to prevent. A red run on a successful publish trains whoever reads it to discount red runs, which is how a real failure gets missed later. Separately, the loop's error message ('still not served after 10 checks') does not distinguish 'not yet visible yet' (propagation lag, likely transient) from 'served but wrong content' (a real mismatch) -- those are different failure classes and should not look identical in the output. Deferred past the OPAG-64 fleet backlog campaign per opum-agent's instruction (2026-09-08); not urgent, does not block any release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The registry-verification loop in release.yml gives win32-arm64 (and any platform) enough total time and backoff to clear ordinary CDN propagation lag without hand-waving the window -- informed by how long 0.4.0 and 0.5.0 actually took to become visible, not guessed

The loop's output/error clearly distinguishes a package that is still not visible (propagation-in-progress, potentially transient) from one that is visible but serves the wrong content (a real mismatch), so a red run always means a real problem
Change is covered by a workflow-level dry run or documented manual verification demonstrating the new window/backoff and the distinguished failure output
